evidence.description: Finite-group decomposition, characters and S3 example

sections.title: What this text studies
sections.text: Representation theory studies algebraic structures through their linear actions on vector spaces. The selected pages introduce modules and invariant subspaces, then specialize to finite groups.

sections.title: Main result in this reading
sections.text: For finite groups over complex numbers, representations decompose into irreducible pieces. Characters record traces and distinguish these decompositions; the regular representation yields the sum-of-squared-dimensions formula.

sections.title: Proof and example
sections.text: Maschke’s proof averages an arbitrary projector to obtain one compatible with the group action. For S3, three conjugacy classes lead to irreducible dimensions 1, 1 and 2, with 1²+1²+2²=6.

sections.title: Hypotheses and version labels
sections.text: Maschke’s general field condition excludes characteristic dividing group order. The inspected PDF also has a 2011 arXiv stamp and 2024 interior date; use its page and section labels when following this guide.

sections.title: Why it matters for moonshine
sections.text: A dimension gives one number; traces of group elements carry finer information. This distinction prepares the reader for graded character series rather than isolated numerical coincidences.
